title: Console: Dedicated staged rollouts UI wireframes + iteration notes
content:
Doc purpose
- Working wireframes + iteration notes for the Dedicated staged rollout UI in Redwood Console.
- Focus is on: stage list, stage detail, gate badges + drill-down, approvals modal, abort flow, and the main error/edge states we expect in beta.
- This is intentionally rough and includes open questions.

Audience
- Console FE/BE (Chloe/Hannah/Felix)
- Product (Marissa/Paula/Lauren)
- SRE (Sean) for failure-mode UX
- Security/RBAC (Kaitlyn) for permissions/microcopy

Scope assumptions (v1 / beta)
- Dedicated pools only (reserved GPU pools).
- Deterministic staged rollouts with gates. A/B experiments are out-of-scope but we should avoid UI dead-ends that make later A/B impossible.
- Operators first; enterprise tenants opt-in. We will show permissions + "contact support" affordances rather than hard-blocking with cryptic 403s.

Information architecture (IA) proposal
Left nav:
- Dedicated
  - Pools
  - Rollouts (NEW)

Alternative IA discussed (not chosen for beta): Pools -> Pool detail -> Rollouts tab.
- Reason: operators want an at-a-glance cross-pool view of rollouts in progress (SRE asks). Also reduces hunting during incidents.

Wireframe set (textual)

Screen 1: Dedicated Rollouts (list view)
Route: /dedicated/rollouts
Primary job: "what is rolling out right now; what’s blocked; what needs approval".

Layout
- Header: "Dedicated rollouts"
- Subtext: "Staged rollouts for reserved pools. Changes apply only within a pool."
- Primary CTA (right): [Create rollout]
- Secondary: [Docs] [API reference] (links only; can hide in beta behind ? menu)

Filters (top row)
- Pool selector (searchable) (optional in beta)
- Status filter chips: In progress | Paused/Hold | Completed | Aborted | Failed
- "Needs my approval" toggle (shows only if user has approve permission; otherwise hidden)

Table columns
- Pool
- Model/Runtime change summary (e.g., "model v3 -> v4" or "runtime config update")
- Current stage (e.g., "Stage 1 (5%)")
- Gate summary badges (mini)
- Status (Running / Hold / Waiting approval / Aborting / Completed)
- Last updated

Gate summary badges (mini)
- Visual: small pill(s) in this order:
  - Latency (p95)
  - Error rate (5xx)
  - Queue depth
  - Utilization
  - Metrics freshness (only shown when unhealthy)
- Badge states:
  - PASS: green outline
  - WARN/HOLD: amber fill (used when rollout is paused due to threshold fail OR missing metrics)
  - FAIL: red fill (used when system has triggered rollback OR gate evaluation explicitly failed)
  - UNKNOWN: gray (used when a gate exists but has not yet evaluated for current stage/window)

Row click -> rollout detail.

Empty states
A) No rollouts exist:
- Title: "No rollouts yet"
- Body: "Create a rollout plan to safely shift traffic through staged gates." (Marissa wants more direct copy)
- CTA: [Create rollout]

B) Filters return none:
- Title: "No results"
- Body: "Try removing filters or selecting a different pool." (no CTA)

Errors
- 403: "You don’t have access to Dedicated rollouts" with guidance:
  - "If you’re an enterprise tenant admin, request enablement." (links to support)
- 5xx: inline retry + link to status page.


Screen 2: Create rollout (wizard)
Route: /dedicated/rollouts/new
Notes:
- This doc focuses on status/approvals, but capturing create flow helps validate what details must exist in detail view.
- We should allow a "template" default stages (5/25/100) and default gates (SRE-signed defaults).

Step 1: Basics
Fields:
- Pool (required) (search, shows tenant)
- Change type (required):
  - Model version change
  - Runtime config change
  - Both
- Summary (required): free text shown in list table (operators want explicit "why")
- Planned start: now | schedule (beta: "now" only)

Step 2: Stages
Stage list editor:
- Each row: Name, Weight %, Evaluation window, Requires approval? (toggle)
- Default template:
  - Stage 0: "Shadow" 0% (optional; default OFF)
  - Stage 1: 5% eval 15m approval required YES
  - Stage 2: 25% eval 30m approval required YES
  - Stage 3: 100% eval 30m approval required YES (question: do we ever require approval at 100%? SRE says yes initially)

Validation rules (UI)
- Total weights must equal 100% (shadow stage excluded if weight=0 and shadow means "no production traffic")
- Stages must be monotonic increasing (5 -> 25 -> 100)
- Evaluation window min 5m max 24h (beta: min 10m recommended)

Step 3: Gates
Gate rows grouped by category:
- Latency p95 (ms) over window
- Error rate (5xx %) over window
- Timeouts (%) over window
- Queue depth (p95)
- GPU utilization (p95)
- Metrics freshness (max age) (special gate)

Default gates toggle:
- "Use recommended defaults" (ON)
- "Customize" (expands)

Step 4: Review + Create
- Summary panel: pool, change summary, stages, gates.
- Warn callout: "If metrics are missing, the rollout will pause for safety." (per ADR behavior)
- CTA: [Create rollout]

Post-create:
- Navigate to detail view.


Screen 3: Rollout detail (overview)
Route: /dedicated/rollouts/{rollout_id}
Primary job: "understand current stage, gate health, and next required action (approve/rollback/abort)."

Header (sticky)
- Breadcrumb: Dedicated rollouts > {Pool name}
- Title: "Rollout: {summary}" (summary is user-entered, not auto)
- Subheader chips:
  - Pool: {pool_id} (copy)
  - Tenant: {tenant name} (copy)
  - Created by: {actor}
  - Plan version: v{n}
- Right side actions:
  - If status Waiting approval and user can approve: [Approve & continue]
  - If status Running and user can abort: [Abort rollout]
  - If status Hold: [View hold reason] (scroll to gates) + [Rollback] (if available)
  - Kebab: "Copy rollout ID", "View audit log"

Top alert region (only when relevant)
- HOLD (amber):
  - Title: "Rollout paused (gate failed)"
  - Body: "Stage 2 requires attention. Traffic remains at 25%."
  - Primary CTA: [Review failing gate]
  - Secondary CTA: [Rollback to previous stage] (if policy allows)

- HOLD (metrics missing) (amber but different copy):
  - Title: "Rollout paused (missing metrics)"
  - Body: "Gate evaluation is blocked because required metrics are stale or unavailable. Traffic remains at current stage."
  - CTA: [View metrics freshness]

- WAITING APPROVAL (blue):
  - Title: "Approval required"
  - Body: "Stage 2 passed gates. Approve to advance to Stage 3 (100%)."
  - CTA: [Approve & continue]

- SYSTEM DEGRADED (red):
  - Title: "Automatic advancement disabled"
  - Body: "Gate evaluator is degraded. Rollouts are held for safety." (align with fail-safe PR_28572)
  - CTA: [View evaluator status]

Tabs (tentative)
- Overview (default)
- Audit log
- JSON (read-only) (operators asked for copy/paste; can be hidden behind feature flag)

Overview tab sections
A) Stage timeline (top)
B) Current stage detail (middle)
C) Gates (expanded view) (below)
D) Activity/audit preview (last 10)


A) Stage timeline component
Visual: horizontal stepper with stage cards.
Each stage card:
- Name (Stage 1)
- Weight (5%)
- State badge:
  - Not started (gray)
  - Running (blue)
  - Evaluating (blue, subtle)
  - Waiting approval (purple)
  - Paused/Hold (amber)
  - Completed (green)
  - Rolled back (red outline)
- Mini gate summary: 3 tiny icons (latency/error/queue) + count of failing gates
- Duration at stage ("14m")
Interaction:
- Click a stage -> scroll to "Current stage detail" and swap that section to show selected stage details (even if past stage).

Iteration note (12/18): Sean asked that "Waiting approval" be visually distinct from "Hold" because oncall action differs.


B) Stage detail panel
Shows for selected stage (default current).
Fields:
- Stage name + weight
- "Traffic allocation" text:
  - "Requests are deterministically assigned to stage variants." (avoid promising perfect percentages)
  - Show actual measured split (if available): "Observed: 24.6%" (optional, later)
- Evaluation window
- Gate evaluation status:
  - "3/4 gates passing" + "Last evaluated 2m ago"
- Next action line:
  - If running/evaluating: "Advances automatically when gates pass" (unless approval required)
  - If waiting approval: "Awaiting approval from: Rollout Approvers (Dedicated)"
  - If hold: "Paused due to: Queue depth gate" (link)

Action buttons (contextual)
- [Approve stage] (if waiting approval)
- [Hold] (manual hold; beta? Paula wants this; SRE says useful)
- [Rollback] (if available and user can)
- [Abort] (always if permissions)

Open question: do we show rollback at stage-level or only as a top-right global action? Current preference: both, but stage-level labeled "Rollback to previous stage".


C) Gates expanded view
Layout: list of gate cards.
Gate card contents:
- Gate name: "Latency p95"
- Threshold: "<= 750ms"
- Window: "15m"
- Current value: "812ms" (with sparkline placeholder)
- Status:
  - PASS (green)
  - FAIL (red) + "exceeded threshold"
  - UNKNOWN (gray) + "insufficient data"
  - STALE (amber) + "metrics older than 3m"
- "View in dashboards" link (points to per-pool gate dashboard)

Gate card secondary details (expand/collapse)
- Query: (read-only) e.g., promql-like or internal query key (beta might hide for enterprise tenants)
- Sample size / request volume (optional)
- Last successful fetch time
- Evaluator run id (debug)

Gate badges (used across UI)
Badge rules:
- Gate badge label should be short: "p95", "5xx", "queue", "util", "fresh"
- Tooltip content pattern:
  - "Latency p95 gate: PASS (642ms <= 750ms)"
  - "Queue depth gate: FAIL (p95 28 > 20)"
  - "Metrics freshness: STALE (age 7m > 3m)"

Iteration note (01/06): We should avoid showing raw units inconsistently. Always show ms/%/count on the value and threshold.


D) Activity preview (mini audit)
"Recent activity" list (latest first):
- {time} {actor} created rollout plan v3
- {time} system advanced to Stage 2
- {time} gate evaluator placed rollout on hold (queue depth)
- Link: [View full audit log]


Screen 4: Approvals modal
Triggered by "Approve & continue".
Primary job: "make approval explicit, show what you are approving, ensure audit clarity".

Modal structure
Title: "Approve stage advancement"
Body:
- "This will advance the rollout from Stage 2 (25%) to Stage 3 (100%) for pool {pool_id}."
- Summary of gate results:
  - Latency p95: PASS (642ms <= 750ms)
  - Error 5xx: PASS (0.08% <= 0.2%)
  - Queue depth: PASS (p95 12 <= 20)
  - Metrics freshness: PASS (age 45s <= 3m)
- "Approval note" (optional text input)

Primary button: [Approve]
Secondary: [Cancel]

Edge states in modal
- If gates are currently FAIL but approval is still possible (should this happen?):
  - Show hard block: "Cannot approve while gates are failing." (preferred)
- If metrics are STALE:
  - Block approval (beta): "Approval disabled because required metrics are stale." (Sean preference)
- If plan version changed since page load:
  - Block with refresh: "This rollout plan was updated. Refresh to view latest." (optimistic concurrency)

Audit requirements (copy)
- Small footer text: "Your name and note will be recorded in the audit log." (Security wants explicit)


Screen 5: Abort rollout flow
Abort is distinct from rollback.
- Abort = stop further changes (traffic stays where it is? or revert? depends on policy). Need clearer naming.

Current proposal:
- Button label: "Abort rollout" (top-right)
- Confirm modal:
  - Title: "Abort rollout?"
  - Body: "Aborting stops the rollout. Traffic remains at the current stage unless you also roll back." (this is confusing; if backend semantics differ, we must update)
  - Options:
    - Primary: [Abort rollout]
    - Secondary: [Cancel]
  - (Optional) checkbox: "Also roll back to previous stable version" (NOT in beta; too complex)

Iteration note (12/11): Paula asked for "Abort and rollback" as a single action during incidents. SRE says we should keep them separate v1 to reduce accidental rollbacks.


Screen 6: Error states + system states
We expect these to be frequent in early dogfood; UI should be extremely explicit.

State: Metrics missing / stale
Where shown:
- Banner at top + specific gate card(s) show STALE.
Copy:
- "Gate evaluation paused: metrics are stale"
- "We haven’t received {metric_name} for {duration}. Rollout will not advance automatically."
Actions:
- [View gate details]
- [Open dashboards]
- [Retry evaluation] (only if backend supports manual trigger; otherwise omit)

State: Evaluator degraded
Where shown:
- Top red banner.
Copy:
- "Automatic stage advancement is disabled"
- "The gate evaluator service is degraded. For safety, this rollout is held at its current stage." (matches fail-safe behavior)
Actions:
- [View evaluator status] (links to internal status panel)
- [Contact on-call] (internal only)

State: Routing / allocation mismatch
Example: the UI says 25% but routing reports different due to pool constraint or guardrails.
Where shown:
- Stage detail panel, under traffic allocation.
Copy:
- "Observed traffic split differs from target"
- "Target: 25%. Observed (last 10m): 12%. This can happen under capacity constraints or guardrails."
Actions:
- [View capacity/guardrails]

State: Permission denied (RBAC)
Pattern: show read-only view where possible.
- If user lacks approve: hide approve buttons and show callout:
  - "You can view this rollout, but you don’t have permission to approve or abort." + link "Request access".
- If user lacks abort but can approve: hide abort button.
- If user lacks view audit log: hide Audit tab; show "Not authorized" if direct nav.

State: Stuck / no progress
If no stage changes in X minutes (SRE alert):
- Show amber banner:
  - "Rollout hasn’t progressed in 45m" (duration dynamic)
  - "Check failing gates or approvals."
- CTA: [Review current stage]


UI strings to confirm with Product
- "Hold" vs "Pause" terminology
  - Current: UI shows "Hold" for system-enforced pause (gate fail / missing metrics), and "Paused" for user-initiated pause.
  - Paula prefers "Paused" everywhere. Sean prefers distinct terms. Need decision.

- "Abort" semantics
  - Clarify if abort stops advancement but keeps current traffic split, or reverts to previous stable stage, or both. Backend definition must be reflected.


Open questions / TODOs
1) Do we show "stage 0 shadow" by default in UI templates?
   - Dedicated teams may interpret "shadow" as duplicate traffic, which we don’t support uniformly. Might confuse.

2) Observed vs target traffic split
   - Routing team says observed split may not be reliable early. If we can’t ship observed in beta, remove references and keep copy general.

3) Gate drill-down depth
   - How much evaluator debug data is safe to show to enterprise tenants? (query strings, run ids)

4) Audit log UX
   - Audit tab should likely support filtering: approvals only, system actions only, plan updates only.
   - Beta can ship a simple chronological list.

5) Accessibility
   - Badge colors cannot be sole signal. Need icons + text (PASS/FAIL) in tooltips and/or inline.

6) Cross-linking to dashboards
   - We need stable deep links per pool_id + rollout_id + stage_id + gate_id.


Quick pseudo-wireframes (ASCII)

List page
[Dedicated rollouts]                              [Create rollout]
Filters: [Status: In progress v] [Pool: search] [Needs my approval]
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Pool        Summary                 Stage        Gates      Status
pool-17     model v4 rollout        Stage 2 25%  p95 5xx q  Waiting approval
pool-22     runtime cfg update      Stage 1 5%   p95 !q     Hold

Detail page
Rollout: "Model v4 rollout"   Pool pool-17   Tenant AcmeCo   v3   [Approve] [Abort]
[BANNER if needed]

Stages:  Stage1 5% (done) -> Stage2 25% (waiting approval) -> Stage3 100% (next)

Stage detail: Stage 2 (25%)
- Window: 30m   Last eval: 2m ago
- Gates: 4/4 PASS
- Next: Approval required

Gates:
[Latency p95] PASS 642ms <= 750ms   [View dashboard]
[5xx rate]    PASS 0.08% <= 0.2%   [View dashboard]
[Queue depth] PASS p95 12 <= 20    [View dashboard]
[Freshness]   PASS age 45s <= 3m   [View dashboard]


Iteration log (high-level)
- 2024-12-04: initial sketch: list + detail + approvals modal.
- 2024-12-11: added explicit HOLD vs WAITING APPROVAL states; added "missing metrics" copy.
- 2024-12-18: added stage stepper; added gate badges + tooltip rules.
- 2025-01-06: tightened units; added evaluator degraded state.
- 2025-01-22: RBAC/read-only patterns updated after Kaitlyn review; added "audit log" tab proposal.

Notes to self (Kenji)
- Keep the UI action-oriented: always a single "next step" CTA when possible.
- Dedicated customers will treat this as change management evidence; audit + clear copy matter more than visual polish.
- Avoid implying that traffic splits are exact; use "target" vs "observed" carefully.
